name: Donne Biryani
instructions: 1. Grind fresh coriander, mint, green chilies, ginger, and garlic into a smooth, vibrant green paste.
2. Marinate the meat (or vegetables) in curd, a portion of the green paste, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
3. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed vessel, add whole spices, and sauté sliced onions until golden brown.
4. Add the marinated ingredients and cook until the meat is tender and the oil separates.
5. Add water in a 1:2 ratio to the rice, bring to a boil, and add the soaked Seeraga Samba rice.
6. Cook covered on low heat until the rice is fluffy and aromatic.
7. Serve hot in traditional dried leaf cups (donne) to absorb the earthy flavor.
description: Donne Biryani is a signature dish from Bengaluru and the surrounding regions of Karnataka. It is named after the 'donne' (leaf cup) it is served in, which imparts a distinct earthy aroma. Unlike the layered Hyderabadi style, this is a 'pulao-style' biryani where the rice is cooked directly in the meat stock and green masala, making it intensely flavorful and popular in local 'military hotels'.
